must_remember: Elliptical polarization represents the most general state of a monochromatic plane electromagnetic wave, where the tip of the electric field vector traces out an ellipse.

The general equation of the polarization ellipse is given by $\frac{E_x^2}{E_{0x}^2} + \frac{E_y^2}{E_{0y}^2} - 2\frac{E_x E_y}{E_{0x} E_{0y}}\cos\delta = \sin^2\delta$, where $\delta$ is the phase difference.
Linear and circular polarizations are special limiting cases of elliptical polarization depending on the amplitudes and phase difference $\delta$.
Right-handed elliptical polarization corresponds to clockwise rotation of the electric vector looking into the beam, while left-handed corresponds to counter-clockwise rotation.
When elliptically polarized light passes through a rotating analyzer, the transmitted intensity varies between a maximum and a non-zero minimum proportional to $a^2$ and $b^2$ respectively.

glossary.meaning: A state of polarization where the tip of the electric field vector describes an ellipse in any fixed plane intersecting, and normal to, the direction of propagation.
The phase angle $\phi_y - \phi_x$ between the two orthogonal electric field components $E_x$ and $E_y$.
The directional sense of rotation of the electric field vector, classified as right-handed (dextro-rotatory) or left-handed (laevo-rotatory).
The principal dimensions of the polarization ellipse corresponding directly to the maximum and minimum electric field vector extremities.
